exercise.name: Waiter Curl
library_steps: Hold one dumbbell upright, both palms flat under its top end.
Keep your elbows at your sides and curl it up to your chest.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing, one dumbbell held upright in front of the hips by both hands under its top end; elbows stay by the sides while it is curled up to chest height (~110 deg of elbow bend) and lowered back to long arms.

setup.target: Feet hip-width, knees soft, trunk upright and still.

Dumbbell vertical, both hands together at the midline under the top end, palms up. Picture: the rig's hands are closed fists, so two fists sit side by side under the top plate with the handle between them (prop_offset).
setup.why: Library step; the open, palms-up hold keeps the forearms supinated.

setup.target: At the sides, pointing down, the whole lift.
setup.why: Library step and ACE curl cue.

movement.start: about 43 deg (hands meet in front of the hips)

muscles.emg: Biceps is the main elbow flexor in standing dumbbell curls (S1); its activity does not depend on hand position (S2). No study on this exact variant was found.
Active in all curls (S1); lower share with the hand supinated than pronated (S2)
muscles.role: Helps bend the elbow; the forearms also hold the open-palm grip.
muscles.surface: Thumb side of the upper forearm.

muscles.role: Keeps the elbows by the sides.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbows leave the sides as the dumbbell rises.
Trunk tips back at the top.

sources.citation: Marcolin G, et al. 2018. Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl. PeerJ 6:e5165.
sources.what_it_gave: Standing curl EMG (dumbbell vs bars), forearm position changes brachioradialis activity; trunk motion policed.

sources.citation: Kleiber T, et al. 2015. Front Physiol 6:215, doi 10.3389/fphys.2015.00215 (EMG of biceps brachii and brachioradialis in elbow flexion by hand position).
sources.what_it_gave: Biceps the same across hand positions; brachioradialis share higher only when pronated.

sources.citation: American Council on Exercise. Exercise Library: Standing Bicep Curl.
sources.what_it_gave: Palms up, elbows close to the sides, hands toward the shoulders, lower slowly.
